author: tersec
content: Not ... so much for or against, but the whole thing is one of the least incentive-aligned parts of Ethereum and this doesn't fix that

author: tersec
content: it used to be incentivized to lie about stake on a node to avoid attestation subnets and, surprise, people did that

author: tersec
content: the max-stake-over-time mechanic punishes people who are operating nodes where stake flows in and out etc etc. but this was all discussed before and this is, whatever

author: tersec
content: oh my favorite, it creates an entirely new kind of "dishonest validator" which is, oops, the database vanished, with the record of previous max stake in it. so now that's "dishonest" too

author: fradamt
content: And yet it largely produces the intended behavior, as defaults often do 🤷‍♂️  Would be fine with removing this completely if distributed reconstruction is adopted, but before that it seems unnecessary.
